title: Pati Patni Aur Woh Do Opens to Mixed Reviews — But NRIs Are Already Circling the Netflix Date
excerpt: Ayushmann Khurrana's chaotic rom-com sequel earned a decent ₹4-5 crore on opening day, but the real battleground for this mid-budget entertainer is the OTT window.
body:
Ayushmann Khurrana has spent the better part of a decade cornering a very specific market: the middle-class Indian film where the humour is situational, the morality is gentle, and the climax rewards the confused husband for being a fundamentally decent man. With Pati Patni Aur Woh Do, directed by Mudassar Aziz, he doubles down on the formula — and depending on which review you read, he either nailed it or sleepwalked through it.

The Premise: Chaos by Committee

The sequel — a "spiritual" follow-up to the 2019 Pati Patni Aur Woh that starred Kartik Aaryan — drops Khurrana into the role of a bumbling forest ranger whose marriage to a progressive wife (Wamiqa Gabbi) gets complicated when Sara Ali Khan and Rakul Preet Singh enter the picture in predictably unpredictable ways. Mudassar Aziz, who also directed the first film, has crafted what multiple reviewers called a "clean, chaotic comedy of errors" — the kind of film where nobody commits an unforgivable sin and the jokes rely more on absurd misunderstandings than cruelty.

The problem, according to Mint's review, is that the film is "curiously disengaged" — it sets up situations without investing in its characters beyond the farce. The Hollywood Reporter India was harsher, calling it "an unfunny infidelity comedy" with "lazy jokes and problematic stereotypes." But audience reactions on social media told a different story: "pure madness," "must-watch," and praise for Rakul Preet's comic timing and Khurrana's ability to hold together an increasingly absurd plot.

The Box Office: Better Than Expected, Worse Than Needed

Opening day numbers tell a complicated story. Depending on the source, Pati Patni Aur Woh Do earned somewhere between ₹3.50 crore and ₹4.90 crore domestically on May 15 — solid for a mid-budget comedy in 2026, but nowhere near blockbuster territory. The worldwide opening was ₹5.62 crore.

For context: the 2019 original opened to ₹9.10 crore. But this is also 1,400% higher than Bollywood's last rom-com sequel (Ginny Weds Sunny 2, which opened to a grim ₹30 lakh). The film's ₹55 crore budget means it needs roughly ₹70 crore total to break even — a target that requires strong legs over the next two weekends.

The Diaspora Play: Netflix Is the Real Opening Day

Here's the thing NRI audiences already know: the film's OTT rights have gone to Netflix. No official streaming date has been announced, but industry trackers expect a 4-6 week theatrical window, putting the Netflix premiere somewhere in late June or early July 2026.

For diaspora viewers who've been burned by limited theatrical runs in the US, UK, and Canada — where mid-budget Hindi films often screen for just one weekend before vanishing — the Netflix window is effectively the real release. And Ayushmann's fanbase skews heavily towards the urban, English-speaking demographic that's already paying for Netflix internationally.

The film is currently running in select theatres across North America through BookMyShow's international distribution. If you can catch it on a big screen, the crowd energy reportedly makes the comedy land better. If not, the wait won't be long.

What's Actually Worth Your Time

Strip away the critical debates and here's the bottom line: Pati Patni Aur Woh Do is a one-time-watch family entertainer with good performances and weak songs. Ayushmann and Wamiqa Gabbi have genuine chemistry. Sara Ali Khan gets to be funny for once. The script won't surprise you if you've seen any Bollywood love-triangle comedy in the last decade, but it won't offend you either — which, for a film about infidelity, is arguably the point.

If you're an NRI scrolling through theatrical options this weekend: it's a safe bet for a date night. If you're waiting for Netflix: you're not missing a life-changing cinematic experience, but you'll have a perfectly pleasant two hours whenever it arrives.
